extracted: Proposed criteria for attributing a death to a drug: exclude other reasonable explanations and establish an understood mechanism, a concentration capable of causing death and a fit with the circumstances. For THC the authors say it may not be possible to provide a minimum blood concentration that might be regarded as causal, because of delays from death to sampling; most laboratories detect 1–2 ng/mL in post-mortem blood, and lower values may reflect use days earlier. A blood THC test, not urine cannabinoids or history alone, is required to link a death to recent use; a cited coroner's discussion advises counting cannabis as contributory only with use within 2 h of the arrest, ideally with blood THC confirmed.
